title.en: Law of radioactive decay, half-life and mean life

hook.en: Nobody can say which kernel will pop next, yet a full pan pops in a predictable way. Single nuclei *decay* at random, but a large number decay by a precise law.

objectives.en: State the law of radioactive decay
Use N = N₀e^(−λt), half-life and mean life

narration.en: Nobody can say which kernel will pop next, yet a full pan pops in a predictable way. Single nuclei decay at random, but a large number decay by a precise law.

title.en: State the law of radioactive decay
Use N = N₀e^(−λt), half-life and mean life

say.en: Nobody can say which kernel will pop next, yet a full pan pops in a predictable way. Single nuclei decay at random, but a large number decay by a precise law. In this lesson: State the law of radioactive decay.
Use N equals N 0e^(- lambda t), half-life and mean life.
Work with activity in becquerel.

body.en: The rate of *decay* is proportional to the number of undecayed nuclei: $dN/dt = -\lambda N$, where λ is the decay constant. Integrating, $N = N_0 e^{-\lambda t}$. The activity $R = \lambda N = R_0 e^{-\lambda t}$ is measured in becquerel (1 Bq = 1 decay per second; 1 Ci = 3.7 × 10¹⁰ Bq). The half-life is $T_{1/2} = \ln 2/\lambda \approx 0.693/\lambda$ and the mean life is $\tau = 1/\lambda \approx 1.44\,T_{1/2}$.

problem.en: A sample has a half-life of 3 h. What fraction is left after 12 h, and after 4 h?

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A sample has a half-life of 3 h. What fraction is left after 12 h, and after 4 h?

say.en: Let us solve this together. A sample has a half-life of 3 hours. What fraction is left after 12 hours, and after 4 hours?
12 hours equals 4 half-lives: N over N 0 equals 1 over 16.
4 hours: N over N 0 equals e^(minus 0.693 times 4 over 3) equals 2^(minus 4 over 3) is approximately 0.397.
So the answer is 1 over 16 after 12 hours; about 0.40 after 4 hours.

problem.en: The half-life of a nuclide is 1386 s. Find λ, the mean life and the time for 75% of a sample to decay.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. The half-life of a nuclide is 1386 s. Find λ, the mean life and the time for 75% of a sample to decay.

say.en: Let us solve this together. The half-life of a nuclide is 1386 seconds. Find lambda, the mean life and the time for 75 percent of a sample to decay.
lambda equals 0.693 over 1386 equals 5.0 times 10 to the power minus 4 seconds to the power minus 1.
tau equals 1/ lambda equals 2000 seconds.
75 percent decayed means 1 over 4 left: 2 half-lives equals 2772 seconds.
So the answer is lambda equals 5 times 10 to the power minus 4 seconds to the power minus 1, tau equals 2000 seconds, t equals 2772 seconds.

explanation.en: 1/8 = (1/2)³: 12 s is three half-lives, so T½ = 4 s.
